Papers / Visual explanation

Learn where to explore from old data.

Empowerment measured from unlabeled data guides online exploration.

Say you have a pile of old data with no rewards or skill labels, and a sparse-reward task to learn online. How can that data tell you where to explore? From the data alone, this paper learns skills that reach futures as different as possible, which gives an estimate of empowerment: roughly how many distinct futures you can reach from a state. In the ant maze, it's high at corridor junctions and low in corners. Online, it becomes an exploration bonus. On antmaze-medium with navigate data, it lifts contrastive RL from 0.29 to 0.43 success and also helps RND and SUPE. Across nine task and dataset pairs, it helps contrastive RL on five and ties on four.

From a state sss, a policy π\piπ can follow any of KKK skills zzz, and you pick one uniformly at random. Call s+s^+s+ the discounted future state: a state some random number of steps ahead, about a hundred on average. pz(s+∣s)p^z(s^+ \mid s)pz(s+∣s) is where skill zzz's futures land, and pˉ\bar ppˉ​ is their average over skills. Empowerment E(s)E(s)E(s) is how much knowing the skill tells you about the future, their mutual information III, under the best policy. You can't run skills on logged transitions (s,a,s′)(s, a, s')(s,a,s′) (state, action, next state), so the method learns Vz(s+∣s)V^z(s^+ \mid s)Vz(s+∣s), a model of pz(s+∣s)p^z(s^+ \mid s)pz(s+∣s), with temporal differences like a value function, while it trains π(a∣s,z)\pi(a \mid s, z)π(a∣s,z) to push the skills' futures apart. A plain empowerment reward can keep the agent parked at junctions. With the max, reaching a junction pays and leaving it to explore costs nothing.
